item.title: On the similarities of economics and ecology
item.description: Can we think of the economy as something analogous to natural ecosystems? This thought emerged to my mind on bear-observation excursion and I immediately started to explore this idea further. I believe that economics and ecology, two seemingly distinct fields, are actually very similar and can tremendously learn from each other. In this article, I will look at the similarities, differences and argue . I will look at some mathematical (no formulas) properties and analyse both from top-down.

item.title: It's the eyes, they never lie
item.description:
Milión červených ruží, chceli by sme celý svet.
V objatí sme ako kruhy, bez začiatku, bez konca.
Vetrom nesieš prvé šifry, pot ma šteklí na perách.
Načo lúštiť povedané? Zamotať sa v riešeniach?
Je to všetko tu, leží ti to na očiach.
Nezľakni sa rezných rán.
Pod nimi je skytým písmom vytlačené,
komu dlžíš ďakujem.

Našiel som ho na najvyššom poschodí

item.title: Places from my dreams
item.description:
Otvoríš oči a spomenieš si, že si tam, kde si vždy chcel byť.
Kam len dovidíš, ti šeptá pokoj do ucha mäkkú uspávanku.
Zabudni, že aj posledný strom raz padne.
Sny sú ako z cukru, vábia s nekalým úmyslom.
Hladné mraky už zdola šplhajú, nie je šanca ujsť.
Len sa dole cez všetko živé prestrieľať.
Je čas ísť späť, na Zem.

Vietor pohne všetkým, iba Tebou nie

item.title: The echo of a distorted cry
item.description:
Snívalo sa mi.
Bol som opäť na tých najkrajších miestach, vôňa levandulí mi opantávala každý zmysel.
Počul známe zvuky, videl veci, čo sa nestali. Čas stál a dal sa ľubovoľne pretáčať.
Tu sa dali porušiť všetky zákony, ani Lorentz nemal žiaden dosah.
Platil by som všetkým za návrat.
No minul som to, a ostalo len, čo som zdedil.

A sme opäť sami

item.title: What drives willingness to pay for renewable electricity in Slovakia?
item.description:
As the climate crisis intensifies, shifting electricity generation to renewable sources has become critical. While engineering solutions continue advancing, understanding consumer preferences and pricing strategies is equally vital for accelerating this transition. As part of my bachelor’s thesis at Erasmus University Rotterdam, I investigated what Slovaks are willing to pay for renewable electricity and which factors influence these preferences.

The Challenge

Slovakia faces a unique situation: the country has substantial potential for renewable energy production (24.4 TWh technical potential vs. 30 TWh current consumption), yet only 23% of electricity comes from renewable sources. With recent energy market crises driven by geopolitical instability, understanding consumer willingness to pay (WTP) for renewable electricity became more urgent than ever. The research posed a central question: Can we quantify what Slovaks are willing to pay for renewable electricity, and can we predict these preferences to enable better pricing strategies?

item.description:
Nasbinals article — research notes

The place

  • Nasbinals: small town, Aubrac plateau, Lozère, southern France
  • Margerie’s family home — visited June–July 2025 (approx. 2 weeks), and again briefly in August
  • Climate: cold even in summer, weak sun, “autumn vibes” in late August; vegetation like September/October in Slovakia
  • Town fills once a year for a trail-running race weekend, then empties again
  • Regular trips to Laguiole for groceries; a second family house referenced as “the other house”

Activities & events

  • Horse riding on Corrida: multiple lessons, several failed attempts, identity crisis around it (“I’m not sure anymore it’s for me”)
  • One riding lesson that “finally worked out”
  • Final morning: bareback ride on Corrida into a stream
  • Trail rides out onto the Aubrac plateau
  • Sunday bike ride — near-crash at 70 km/h (insect in mouth on descent), exhausting day in full sun
  • Wolf park visit — described as “really nice”
  • Waterfall visit with Margerie — photographs taken, “amazing”
  • Dinners at L’Annexe (regular, noted as expensive but good)
  • Dinner with extended family (noted as nice)

Emotional arc in Nasbinals

  • Arrived with mixed feelings: valued the place and hospitality, couldn’t fully reciprocate emotionally
  • Identity crisis: coffee machine breaking, failed rides, sense of things “not being in the stars”
  • Gradual settling: the riding lesson that worked, the bareback ride, the last dinner
  • Left with something heavy — “sad leave” recorded in journal
  • Even while in Venice days later: “missing Nasbinals and Margerie”

The rest of the trip (briefly)

  • Route: Košice → Zurich (stopover with friend Rici, bike ride, pizza) → Nasbinals → Briançon → Col du Granon → Torino → Padova → Venice → Croatia
  • Col du Granon: Tour de France climb above Briançon, solo ride, “very exciting”; minor mishap with torn sleeve
  • Torino: evening walk; pigeon incident
  • Padova: bought camera lens (“spent a lot of money”), brutal heat
  • Venice: “amazing, despite me missing Nasbinals and Margerie”
  • Croatia: family holiday, rest, reading (3 books), beach, bike rides, watched Tour de France; mixed feelings about crowds

Solo travel reflection (from July 9 journal entry)

  • First ever solo road trip
  • “The solo travel was my first ever and it has shown me how much I enjoy it”
  • Liked: personal regime, freedom, commitment, the activities
  • Qualifications: “slightly repetitive,” compared too much to prior year, a fight with Margerie
  • Trip became a counterweight to the “I have to leave Košice” theme running through 2025

The memory transformation (May 2026 sources)

  • Nostalgia surfaced unprompted during a cottage walk, May 2026
  • Triggered again when picking up tupperware from Margerie after the relationship ended
  • Direct quote from journal (2026-05-17): “My brain started to keep the Nasbinals memory as some fever dream. Everything from it feels so distant now but so beautiful. I keep a lot of it as a great memory and I can feel it will impact who I am and my future artistic endeavours. I will keep returning there and I will keep grounding myself in that place. For some reasons those two weeks were so magical that I will want to keep going back metaphysically. Maybe I will visit it one day again. For now, it must live in my memories, never to be forgotten.”
  • He distinguishes nostalgia for the place from longing for Margerie specifically

Tone of voice — observed from existing articles

  • Opens with a personal hook that drops straight into experience, no preamble
  • Honest about difficulty and ambivalence — doesn’t sanitise
  • Short punchy sentences mixed with longer flowing ones
  • Reflective without being overwrought; philosophy earns its place
  • Concrete sensory detail used sparingly for grounding
  • Doesn’t explain emotions — names them and moves on
  • Endings carry quiet weight, often circling back to the opening image
  • Wolf-tracking article structure: stat grid + named sections + blockquotes for standout moments
  • Climate ambassador article: clean, direct, professional but personal
  • Economics/ecology draft: more analytical, uses italics for definitions, looser structure
  • Photography pages (Slovak): highly poetic, abstract, metaphor-heavy — closest to v2 register
